## Introduction

For week 7, I chose three books under data sicence and statistical learning. I manually created an HTML file and a JSON file that had the same book info.

The goal is to import both files into R, change them into data frames, and compare results.

## 1. Load Packages

```{r}
library(rvest)
library(jsonlite)
```

## 2. Import HTML Data

\- `rvest` lets me to extract the table from my HTML file.

```{r}
html_page <- read_html("books.html")

html_df <- html_page |>
  html_element("table") |>
  html_table()

html_df <- as.data.frame(html_df)

html_df
```

## 3. Import JSON Data

\-`jsonlite` lets me read the JSON file and convert it into a data frame.

```{r}
json_df <- fromJSON("books.json")

json_df <- as.data.frame(json_df)

json_df
```

## 4. Data Frames Comparison

I had to standardize the column order and data types before verifying if the two data frames coincide.

```{r}
columns <- c("Title", "Authors", "Year",
             "Publisher", "Edition")

html_df <- html_df[, columns]
json_df <- json_df[, columns]

html_df$Year <- as.integer(html_df$Year)
json_df$Year <- as.integer(json_df$Year)

html_df$Edition <- as.integer(html_df$Edition)
json_df$Edition <- as.integer(json_df$Edition)

rownames(html_df) <- NULL
rownames(json_df) <- NULL

identical(html_df, json_df)
```

## 5. Conclusion

Ultimately, the assignment showed me how HTML and JSON can indicate identical information using different frameworks.

While HTML formats data within a table, JSON organizes the information as structured entities.

After importing and standardizing both datasets, I am able to compare their contents in R to ensure that the information is consistent throughout formats.
